entities.summary:
Miguel Corte-Real, a Portuguese explorer, embarked on an expedition to chart the coast of Labrador in 1502. He disappeared under unclear circumstances, leaving behind a significant body of work that would be studied by later cartographers. Corte-Real's disappearance occurred during a period of increased maritime exploration and conflict between European powers and indigenous peoples in North America. His legacy has been the subject of some debate among historians, with some attributing his disappearance to deliberate abandonment or others suggesting that he may have been lost at sea due to navigational errors.

Corte-Real's disappearance had a lasting impact on the exploration of North America, as it highlighted the risks and challenges faced by early European explorers. His work, although incomplete, provided valuable insights into the geography and natural resources of the region, influencing the development of later maps and cartographic techniques.

The disappearance of Miguel Corte-Real has also been seen as a symbol of the perils faced by explorers in the early modern period, who often faced hostile reception from indigenous peoples and harsh environmental conditions. His story serves as a reminder of the complexity and uncertainty of historical events, and the need for careful consideration of the sources and contexts in which they are presented.

In terms of his legacy, Corte-Real's disappearance is often seen as a cautionary tale about the dangers of hubris and overconfidence in exploration. His story has been interpreted in various ways by historians, with some seeing it as a example of the risks of unchecked ambition, while others have highlighted the bravery and determination that characterized his expeditions.
